newsitem.title: USA: WHX workers win benefit ruling in Ohio.
newsitem.headline: WHX workers win benefit ruling in Ohio.

text.p: An Ohio court ruled Monday that unemployment benefits cannot be denied to nearly 4,000 steelworkers on strike at WHX Corp, a decision that reversed an earlier state ruling.

Belmont County Common Pleas Judge Jennifer Sargus ruled that WHX should have extended its former contract with the United Steelworkers before the union's work stoppage, which began October 1 when the pact expired.
Because the company did not extend the contract, workers are entitled to unemployment benefits, Sargus said.
Attorneys for WHX said they would appeal Sargus's ruling.
The strike against the Wheeling, W.Va., steelmaker has idled eight plants in Ohio, West Virginia and Pennsylvania. The dispute centers around pensions.
The union has demanded that WHX establish a defined benefit plan. Company negotiators have refused and instead have offered to enhance the current defined contribution plan.
Negotiations have taken place periodically over the past several months but have ended without a resolution. No further talks are scheduled.
Sargus's ruling reverses a November 22 ruling by the state of Ohio that said workers were not entitled to unemployment benefits because the work stoppage was a strike, not a lockout.
Pennsylvania and West Virginia also recently ruled that workers were not entitled to unemployment benefits. Union attorneys have filed appeals, which are pending.
The union filed for unemployment benefits last year after the strike began.
